narrative: Fire dominated the signal this cycle: a global synthesis traces the fire crisis to compounding human and bioclimatic drivers, while work on post-fire reptile activity and nitrogen-fuelled forest recovery shows how regimes reshape ecosystems. Climate stories centred on drought, with projected intensification of risk for rainfed crops, metric choice biasing estimates of ecosystem water limitation, and uncertain futures for Europe's mountain flora. Movement and connectivity featured prominently, from step-selection predictions of connectivity to evidence that human presence drives mammal avoidance behaviour and that planted woodlands improve connectivity. Trophic and herbivory papers examined how algal traits steer energy transfer and how herbivory shifts between day and night and along succession. On the conservation side, biased extinction-risk assessments in Antarctica and the value of other effective area-based conservation measures stood out, alongside new tools such as Bacpipe and machine-learning detection of wildlife trade.
